## What you should be able to do tonight

- Derive the Black-Scholes partial differential equation from a delta-hedged self-financing portfolio.
- Say exactly where the stock's expected return cancels, and what that cancellation depends on.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Finish the derivation: apply Itô to the option value, form the portfolio that is long the option and short delta shares, observe that the Brownian term cancels when delta is the partial derivative, and conclude that the remaining deterministic portfolio must earn the risk-free rate. Write it out cleanly, once, and keep the page.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Identify what the cancellation needs: continuous rebalancing, continuous paths, and a known volatility. Each failure of those three is a real hedging cost, and weeks 37 and 39 measure the first two.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Solve the PDE for a European call by recognising it as a heat equation after a change of variables, or read the transformation in the MIT 15.450 notes. You do not need to do the transformation from memory, but you should have seen why it works.
:::
:::
